content:
In May this year, the Google Health app was launched alongside the brand-new, affordable Google Fitbit Air health tracker series.

Initially, Google Health only offered a one-way Apple Health integration. The app can read and import health data recorded by iPhone, Apple Watch, and other HealthKit-enabled apps, but it cannot write Fitbit data back to Apple Health.

Today's iOS app update for Google Health fills in the missing half of this connection.

Google Health can now not only read data from HealthKit but also write data into Apple Health.

The update notes for version 5.05 specifically highlight the Apple Health sync feature:

Workout records, sleep, vitals, steps, and other Fitbit data can now be made available to other HealthKit-compatible apps according to the permission settings chosen by the user.

Before this update, users who wanted to transfer Fitbit data to Apple Health generally had to rely on third-party sync tools, or establish an indirect connection through other services.

This gap can be traced back as far as 2014. Shortly after Apple introduced HealthKit in iOS 8, Fitbit stated it had no plans to support that platform.

Version 5.05 also adds the Smart Health Links feature, allowing users to share medical records with healthcare professionals or family members.

The new version of the Google Health iOS app is now available on the App Store. For more information about Google Health, visit 9to5Google.
